name: whole_body_tripod_step_amplitude_ladder_v1
description: Whole-body ALTERNATING TRIPOD step-in-place LIFT-AMPLITUDE LADDER from the champion stand pose (final tick of rl_stand_20260812_145534.csv, the same home whole_body_tripod_step_in_place_v1 uses). Purpose: whole_body_tripod_step_in_place_v1 proved a three-foot swing is electrically and posturally safe, but at 15 mm commanded lift the wide camera saw NO clearance -- stance droop appears to eat the whole command. This ladder walks the commanded lift up until feet visibly leave the floor, so we learn the smallest command that actually produces clearance -- the swing height every gait must use. Sequence at 10 Hz: 3 s settle at the six-foot stand, then for each lift amplitude in 15, 25, 35, 45 mm one tripod A (L0,L2,L4) cycle followed by one tripod B (L1,L3,L5) cycle; each cycle lifts the tripod over 1.2 s (smoothstep in foot height), HOLDS 3.0 s CLEAR at peak lift so the wide camera cannot miss the lifted state, lowers 1.2 s down the same path, then dwells 1.0 s on all six feet. 54.1 s total (542 ticks) -- 3 s settle plus eight 6.4 s half-cycles, one tick trimmed off the final dwell. THREE FEET ARE OFF THE GROUND AT ONCE and never more: the other three legs hold the stand pose exactly, the two tripods never overlap, and the trajectory starts and ends at the full six-foot stand. NO HIP-YAW MOTION AND NO BODY TRANSLATION AT ALL -- yaw is fixed at the stand value on every leg and each lift is a pure VERTICAL foot displacement at constant radial reach, solved with the repo's two-link IK (safe_zero.ik_hip_knee); radial drift is <0.02 mm (2-decimal joint rounding) so each lifted foot goes straight up and comes straight back down onto its own footprint. Per-leg joint travel grows with the rung: about -10.9 deg hip / +1.8 deg knee at 15 mm up to about -29.9 deg hip / +2.2 deg knee at 45 mm. NOTE ON SPEED: peak commanded joint rate is ~37 deg/s on the 45 mm rung (1.5x the mean of a 1.2 s smoothstep), marginally ABOVE the default 400 counts/s (~35 deg/s) profile speed, so on the top rungs the servo may trail the command by a few tens of ms; the 3.0 s hold absorbs that entirely and the measured clearance is read at the hold, not during the ramp. Peak per-tick step is ~3.7 deg at 10 Hz. Soft torque 700; loaded current budget 2.0 A tripping after three consecutive readings above it; hard ceiling 3.0 A. Robot ON THE GROUND (unsupported), operator watching, hands ready; requires force=true.
